title: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN (Dan 5:24–28)
speaker: Daniel
description: Writing on the palace wall which Daniel reads as: God has numbered the kingdom and ended it; the king is weighed and found wanting; the kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians.
in_text_interpretation: Daniel's reading (5:26–28) and the narrated sequel that night (5:30–31).

interpretations.label: Fulfilled that night in the fall of Babylon
interpretations.summary: The kingdom of Belshazzar ended when Babylon passed to Cyrus in October 539 BC.

referents.referent: Babylon given to the Medes and Persians

interpretations.label: Weights and wordplay
interpretations.summary: As nouns the words name weights — a mina, a shekel and half-pieces — which Daniel reinterprets as verbs; parsîn also puns on "Persia". If the half-pieces are two half-shekels the total is 62 shekels, the age given for Darius the Mede. This is a reading of the words, not a fulfillment claim.
